chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad from 'Abd al-Samad ibn Bashir said:

Muhammad ibn al-Qasim al-Hannat asked him, saying: 'May Allah rectify you, I sell food to a man for a specified term. I come [to collect] and the food has changed in price, so he says, 'You do not have dirhams with me.' He said: 'Take from him at the price of that day.' He said: 'Do I understand, may Allah rectify you, that it is my food which he bought from me?' He said: 'Do not take from him until he sells it and gives you [the money].' He said: 'May my nose be rubbed in dust, he permitted me [to do so], so I returned to him, and he made it strict upon me.'

key_terms.أَرْغَمَ اَللَّهُ أَنْفِي: May my nose be rubbed in dust (expression of humility or emphasis)
key_terms.بِسِعْرِ يَوْمِهِ: At the price of that day

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on taking back food sold for deferred payment if the buyer cannot pay the money?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the mechanics of *bay' al-salam* (forward sale) by distinguishing between taking the specific commodity as debt repayment versus waiting for the buyer to liquidate the asset and pay the cash price. The narrator’s concluding remark, 'May God humiliate me, I was granted leniency but I rejected it,' highlights the scholarly nuance between the permissibility of taking the goods directly versus the stricter requirement of monetary settlement, reflecting the practical legal reasoning of the Imams in commercial transactions.
